newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus bourse index hits all-time low.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bourse index hits all-time low.

text.p: The Cyprus stock exchange fell to an all-time low on Wednesday and analysts said it may take government intervention to reverse the trend.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) all-share index tumbled by 0.87 percent on Wednesday, closing at 75.33 points. The CSE has declined by 3.37 percent since Friday's close.
"We cannot know where it will stop," said Christodoulos Ellinas, a partner at Share Link Stockbrokers in Nicosia.

"The political issue has affected the exchange and there have also been delays by the government to take measures to rejuvenate the CSE which it promised to take months ago," he said. "The market needs something new."

Some traders said the market is still feeling the effects of the missile crisis which broke out earlier this month when Cyprus announced it would purchase anti-aircraft missiles and Turkey threatened a military strike to stop their deployment.
Market players are placing their hopes in a government announcement expected on Thursday of an incentive package to spur investor interest in the exchange.
The finance minister is due to meet with the board of the bourse on Thursday morning.
"We are hoping for incentives but I cannot predict what the government will say," a CSE economist told Reuters. Other economists speculated that tax incentives would be announced after the meeting.
Losses have been registered in all seven sub-indices since Friday. The approved investment sector took a hammering. Its sub index lost 7.86 percent between Friday and Wednesday.
Banking stocks, the strongest on the market, dropped 2.14 percent. Shares of the Bank of Cyprus retreated 7 cents to close at 317.5. Popular Bank shares closed at 312.5, down 5.5 cents from Friday.
The Hellenic Bank closed at 259, down three cents, while the Universal Savings Bank bucked the trend to gain four cents, closing at 142.

In the insurance sector, Universal Life insurance made gains of 13.5 cents on trading which moved in relatively low volumes. Paneuropean Insurance dropped 10 cents to close at 102.5. Interamerican lost nine cents, closing at 88.5. Philiki Insurance, which closed at 212 on Friday, closed at 205 on Wednesday.
Cement producer Vassiliko declined 10.5 cents to 138.5. Beer and wine producer Keo closed the day at 103, a 10-month low and five cents lower than Friday.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 33 cents from 31.5 cents on Friday.
